struct.title: Cryo-EM structure of the undecorated barbed end of filamentous beta/gamma actin

pubmed.rcsb_pubmed_abstract_text: The release of inorganic phosphate (P <sub>i </sub>) from actin filaments constitutes a key step in their regulated turnover, which is fundamental to many cellular functions. The mechanisms underlying P <sub>i </sub> release from the core and barbed end of actin filaments remain unclear. Here, using human and bovine actin isoforms, we combine cryo-EM with molecular-dynamics simulations and in vitro reconstitution to demonstrate how actin releases P <sub>i </sub> through a 'molecular backdoor'. While constantly open at the barbed end, the backdoor is predominantly closed in filament-core subunits and opens only transiently through concerted amino acid rearrangements. This explains why P <sub>i </sub> escapes rapidly from the filament end but slowly from internal subunits. In a nemaline-myopathy-associated actin variant, the backdoor is predominantly open in filament-core subunits, resulting in accelerated P <sub>i </sub> release and filaments with drastically shortened ADP-P <sub>i </sub> caps. Our results provide the molecular basis for P <sub>i </sub> release from actin and exemplify how a disease-linked mutation distorts the nucleotide-state distribution and atomic structure of the filament.
